title: Food Chains: Who Eats Whom?
summary: Energy starts with the Sun and passes along a chain of plants and animals.

steps.title: Plants make food
sentences: Almost every food chain starts with a plant.
Plants use sunlight, water and air to make their own food, so we call them producers.
The Sun is the original source of the energy.

steps.title: Eaters
sentences: Animals cannot make their own food, so they are called consumers.
Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat other animals, and omnivores eat both.
A grasshopper eats grass, a frog eats the grasshopper, and a snake eats the frog.

steps.title: Cleaning up
sentences: When plants and animals die, tiny living things called decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria, break them down.
This returns nutrients to the soil, which helps new plants grow.

steps.title: Webs and balance
sentences: In real life animals eat many things, so food chains join up into a food web.
If one kind of animal disappears, others in the web are affected.
That is why protecting nature, even small insects, matters.

facts: Only about ten percent of the energy at one level of a food chain reaches the next level.
A single tiger needs a large forest because it sits near the top of a long food chain.
Mushrooms are not plants: fungi form their own kingdom of life.

quiz.q: What do we call plants in a food chain?
quiz.why: Plants make food from sunlight, so they are producers.

quiz.q: An animal that eats only plants is a...

quiz.why: Fungi and bacteria break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.
